The AI chip supply chain in brief

The fifteen stages that turn sand and software into an AI accelerator: who leads each one, how concentrated it is, and where China and the United States stand.

Download the PDF 4 pagesRead the full chain

Updated 25 October 2026 · Every figure is cited in the chapter each card links to

The chain at a glance

8 of 15 stages are rated Extreme concentration, meaning three or fewer firms could supply each of them today, or one firm holds more than half of it.

StageConcentrationSubstitutabilityWho leads
  1. 01Chip Design, EDA and IPExtremeHardSynopsys US, Cadence US
  2. 02Silicon and WafersHighModerateShin-Etsu Handotai JP, SUMCO JP
  3. 03Chemicals, Gases and PhotoresistHighModerateJSR JP, Tokyo Ohka Kogyo JP
  4. 04LithographyExtremeVery hardASML NL, Nikon JP
  5. 05Photomasks and PelliclesExtremeHardAGC JP, Hoya JP
  6. 06Deposition and EtchHighModerateApplied Materials US, Lam Research US
  7. 07Metrology and InspectionHighModerateKLA US, Applied Materials US
  8. 08Transistors and the Front EndExtremeHardTSMC TW, Intel US
  9. 09Foundries and FabsExtremeHardTSMC TW, Intel Foundry US
  10. 10Memory and HBMExtremeHardSK hynix KR, Samsung KR
  11. 11Advanced PackagingExtremeModerateTSMC TW, Intel US
  12. 12Substrates and PCBsExtremeHardAjinomoto JP, Nitto Boseki JP
  13. 13Test and AssemblyHighModerateAdvantest JP, Teradyne US
  14. 14Systems and NetworkingHighModerateNvidia US, Broadcom US
  15. 15Data Centers and PowerHighModerateGE Vernova US, Hitachi Energy CH

Concentration counts the firms that credibly supply a stage. Every stage rates Extreme or High. Substitutability rates how hard it would be for a well-funded state or firm to build an alternative: Very hard, Hard or Moderately hard.

The fifteen stages

In the order a chip is made.

01Stage 1 of 15

Chip Design, EDA and IP

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA sell the software used to design every leading-edge AI accelerator. In 2025 they took over 85 percent of an $18 billion market, licensed blocks included.

Who leads

  • Synopsys US90%+ of the timing-signoff market at advanced nodes as of 2026
  • Cadence US55-60% of the hardware emulator market at advanced nodes as of 2026
  • Siemens EDA US85%+ of physical verification, the final layout check, at advanced nodes as of 2026

China

China designs its own AI accelerators, but Huawei's most powerful chip in 2026, the Ascend 950, delivers about half the computing performance of Nvidia's H100 from 2022, on Epoch AI's estimate. CSIS found that as of 2025 Chinese design tools were still far from replacing the full range of advanced capabilities US firms offer, especially for 5 nm and 3 nm chips.

United States

Synopsys and Cadence, the two largest design-software vendors by 2025 revenue, are American.

Read the chapter, with its sources

02Stage 2 of 15

Silicon and Wafers

High concentrationModerately hard to substitute

Firms based in Japan, Taiwan, Germany and South Korea make most 300 mm wafers used for advanced chips. China makes most polysilicon, almost all of it for solar cells.

Who leads

  • Shin-Etsu Handotai JPIts parent's electronics materials segment, wafers included, had ¥1,015.7bn of sales in the year to March 2026
  • SUMCO JP¥409,670m of net sales in 2025
  • GlobalWafers TWNT$60.6bn revenue in 2025

China

China made about 93 percent of the world's polysilicon in 2023, and an estimated 98 percent of China's output was solar-grade. Eswin, mainland China's largest maker of 300 mm wafers, says it had about 7.7 percent of world 300 mm shipments in the first half of 2026.

United States

None of the five largest wafer makers in 2025 was American. GlobalWafers of Taiwan won CHIPS awards of up to $406 million in December 2024 for wafer plants in Texas and Missouri.

Read the chapter, with its sources

03Stage 3 of 15

Chemicals, Gases and Photoresist

High concentrationModerately hard to substitute

Japanese companies held 78 percent of world photoresist sales in 2023. Supply of chip chemicals, gases and metals has been disrupted three times since 2019.

Who leads

  • JSR JPA vehicle of the state-backed Japan Investment Corporation bought 84.36% of JSR in April 2024
  • Tokyo Ohka Kogyo JPResist maker with ¥139,668m of sales in the first half of fiscal 2026
  • Air Liquide FR€2,465m of electronics revenue in 2025, 9.1% of group sales

China

In March 2026 the Chinese resist maker Hubei Dinglong said China had yet to reach large-scale production of advanced resist for 248 nm, 193 nm or extreme-ultraviolet printing. Since August 2023 China has required licenses to export gallium and germanium.

United States

In photoresist, American companies ranked a distant second to Japanese companies by sales in 2023. In 2021 JSR of Japan agreed to buy Inpria, an Oregon-based US maker of resist for extreme ultraviolet.

Read the chapter, with its sources

04Stage 4 of 15

Lithography

Extreme concentrationVery hard to substitute

ASML, a Dutch firm, is the only maker of extreme ultraviolet scanners, the machines that print the finest layers of a chip. It sold 48 of them in 2025.

Who leads

  • ASML NL100% of EUV (extreme ultraviolet) systems sold in 2025
  • Nikon JP22 new chip lithography systems in the year to March 2026
  • Canon JP234 chip lithography systems in 2025, 188 of them i-line and 46 KrF

China

In September 2025 CSIS judged that EUV remained firmly out of reach for China despite massive state investment. SMEE, a Chinese scanner maker, had its largest share in i-line tools, the coarsest kind, and even there held 4 percent of the world market as of 2025.

United States

No American firm makes scanners, CSET found in 2021. But a US rule published in October 2023 covers immersion scanners with an alignment error between 1.5 nm and 2.4 nm bound for advanced chipmaking if they hold any American-made parts. The US entity list also requires a license to supply the firms it names.

Read the chapter, with its sources

05Stage 5 of 15

Photomasks and Pellicles

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

Only three firms in the world make the blank plates for the masks used to print the finest layers of leading-edge chips. Japan's AGC and Hoya are two of them.

Who leads

  • AGC JPRanks itself No.2 worldwide in EUV mask blanks on its own fiscal 2026 estimates
  • Hoya JPSaid in its 2026 report that its share of mask blanks is exceptionally high
  • Lasertec JPLaunched the world's first tool that inspects patterned EUV masks at the scanner's own wavelength in 2019

China

As of 2026 SMIC runs two mask shops of its own in Shanghai. No Chinese firm appears in CSET's 2025 market shares for electron-beam mask writers, the machines that draw the pattern onto a mask.

United States

In December 2025 Photronics called itself a leading worldwide maker of photomasks. As of 2026 KLA sells tools that inspect EUV masks and optical masks, the quartz masks used with deep ultraviolet light.

Read the chapter, with its sources

06Stage 6 of 15

Deposition and Etch

High concentrationModerately hard to substitute

Deposition and etch tools build a chip layer by layer. China-based toolmakers' share of deposition tools rose from 2 to 7 percent between 2019 and 2024, by CSET's count.

Who leads

  • Applied Materials US82.4% of physical vapor deposition tools in 2025, by CSET's count from TechInsights data
  • Lam Research US51.2% of conductor etch tools in 2025
  • Tokyo Electron JP55.9% of dielectric etch tools in 2025

China

Chinese toolmakers held 12.4 percent of dry etch in 2025, according to CSET's analysis of TechInsights data. They held 2.6 percent of atomic layer deposition that year, by the same count.

United States

A December 2024 US rule lists some dry etch, atomic layer deposition and deep-hole deposition tools as controlled exports. Its foreign direct product rule reaches some tools built outside the United States.

Read the chapter, with its sources

07Stage 7 of 15

Metrology and Inspection

High concentrationModerately hard to substitute

KLA, an American firm, held 56.8 percent of the market for tools that measure and inspect wafers in 2025, by CSET's count.

Who leads

  • KLA US56.8% of process control tools in 2025 by CSET's count
  • Applied Materials US11.2% of process control tools in 2025
  • Lasertec JP6.4% of process control tools in 2025

China

Chinese firms held 0.7 percent of the world market for tools that measure and inspect wafers in 2025, by CSET's count. Skyverse, a Shenzhen maker of inspection and metrology tools, reported 2,053,298,171.74 yuan of revenue in 2025, up 48.75 percent on 2024.

United States

In 2025 the American firm KLA was the world's largest maker of metrology and inspection tools. Citing Gartner, KLA puts its 2024 share at 56.5 percent, 6.5 times its nearest rival's share.

Read the chapter, with its sources

08Stage 8 of 15

Transistors and the Front End

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

Only TSMC, Intel and Samsung make 2 nm-class transistors in volume. TSMC plans A14 for 2028, with more than 20 percent higher logic density than its 2 nm-class N2.

Who leads

  • TSMC TWN2 in volume production since 4Q25, TSMC's first nanosheet node
  • Intel US18A in high-volume production in the United States, as of 2026
  • Samsung Foundry KRStarted initial production of its 3 nm gate-all-around process in June 2022

China

SMIC makes chips on its N+3 process, which SemiAnalysis measured in June 2026 at 113.4 million transistors per square millimeter, against 107.7 million for TSMC's N6. It builds its tightest layers in several patterning steps because it cannot buy an extreme-ultraviolet scanner.

United States

In August 2025 Intel called itself the only chipmaker that both develops and manufactures leading-edge logic chips in the United States. It says its 18A process brought gate-all-around transistors and backside power to market together in 2025.

Read the chapter, with its sources

09Stage 9 of 15

Foundries and Fabs

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

TSMC's six largest plants are all in Taiwan. In 2025 they could make more than 13 million wafers a year, out of more than 17 million for the whole company.

Who leads

  • TSMC TW79% of its wafer revenue from 7 nm and below, 3Q26
  • Intel Foundry US$5.8bn segment revenue in 2Q26, only $293m of it from outside customers
  • Samsung Foundry KROver $37bn planned in Texas (CHIPS award, Dec 2024)

China

Georgetown University's CSET reported in June 2024 that Huawei's Ascend 910B AI chip is believed to be made on SMIC's 7 nm-class N+2 process. But SemiAnalysis judged in April 2025 that most 910B and 910C chips were made at TSMC.

United States

The US government agreed in August 2025 to buy a passive 9.9 percent stake in Intel, with no board seat. Announcing the deal, Intel called itself the only chipmaker that both develops and manufactures leading-edge logic chips in the United States. Intel Foundry lost $2.089 billion in the second quarter of 2026.

Read the chapter, with its sources

10Stage 10 of 15

Memory and HBM

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

SK hynix, Samsung and Micron make nearly all high bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked memory beside AI chips. SK hynix took 63.2 percent of HBM revenue in 2025.

Who leads

  • SK hynix KR63.2% of HBM revenue in 2025
  • Samsung KR19.3% of HBM revenue in 2025
  • Micron US17.4% of HBM revenue in 2025

China

The Institute for Progress estimated in October 2025 that China would make virtually no HBM that year. Huawei said in September 2025 that its Ascend 950 chips would use two HBM designs of its own, without saying who would manufacture the memory.

United States

Micron is the only American HBM maker. As of October 2026, License Exception HBM lets US and allied exporters ship HBM below 3.3 GB per second per square millimeter without a license, including to China when the chip designer buys it directly and it goes straight to the packaging site.

Read the chapter, with its sources

11Stage 11 of 15

Advanced Packaging

Extreme concentrationModerately hard to substitute

Epoch AI estimates that in 2025 Nvidia, Google, AMD and Amazon used around 90 percent of the capacity for CoWoS, TSMC's packaging for AI chips.

Who leads

  • TSMC TWCoWoS packaging used by Nvidia, Google, AMD and Amazon in 2025
  • Intel USFoveros 3D packaging in volume at Rio Rancho, New Mexico, since January 2024
  • ASE Technology TWNT$389.2B assembly, test and materials revenue, 2025

China

Chinese firms had 5.3 percent of the market for fabrication tools built for advanced packaging in 2025, by CSET's analysis of TechInsights data. Between 2019 and 2024 they gained 5 percentage points of share in test tools but lost share in bonding and other conventional assembly and packaging tools.

United States

Intel opened Fab 9 in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, in January 2024 to make its Foveros 3D packages in volume. Amkor broke ground in October 2025 on a $7B packaging and test campus in Peoria, Arizona, and expects production to start in early 2028.

Read the chapter, with its sources

12Stage 12 of 15

Substrates and PCBs

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

Ajinomoto, a Japanese food company, told investors in June 2026 that it holds over 95 percent of the market for the insulating film inside high-end chip packages.

Who leads

  • Ajinomoto JPTold investors in June 2026 that its build-up film has held over 95% of its market since launch
  • Nitto Boseki JPClaimed an overwhelming advantage in low thermal expansion glass in its 2025 integrated report
  • Ibiden JPSaid in May 2026 that it typically takes close to 100% of each new generation of interposer-type substrates at launch

China

TTM, an American circuit board maker, said in its annual report for 2025 that its circuit board competitors are mostly based in China and Taiwan. Nitto Boseki, a Japanese glass fiber maker, said in its 2025 integrated report that Chinese and Taiwanese companies are aggressively catching up with it in the special glass sector.

United States

The White House's 2021 supply chain review listed no American firm among the key substrate makers. In December 2024 the US Commerce Department finalized an award of up to $75 million to Absolics, an affiliate of Korea's SKC, for a glass substrate plant in Covington, Georgia.

Read the chapter, with its sources

13Stage 13 of 15

Test and Assembly

High concentrationModerately hard to substitute

Testing finds bad chips before they go into an expensive package. Japan's Advantest took about 65 percent of 2025 spending on chip testers, by its own estimate.

Who leads

  • Advantest JPAbout 65% of the tester market in 2025, by its own estimate
  • Teradyne US$2.52bn of semiconductor test revenue in 2025, service included
  • ASE TWRan 8,348 testers in Q2 2026, up from 6,797 a year earlier

China

Georgetown's CSET, analyzing TechInsights data, finds that between 2019 and 2024 Chinese toolmakers gained 5 percentage points of world market share in test tools and 4 points in fabrication tools built for advanced packaging. But they lost share in bonding and other conventional assembly and packaging tools.

United States

American firms held 23.5 percent of the market for test tools in 2025 and Japanese firms 63.0 percent, by CSET's analysis of TechInsights data. Amkor raised its planned investment in an Arizona packaging and test campus to $7 billion in October 2025. In June 2026 it announced a long-term partnership with TSMC, which will buy packaging and test services from it in Arizona.

Read the chapter, with its sources

14Stage 14 of 15

Systems and Networking

High concentrationModerately hard to substitute

Nvidia's and AMD's racks wire 72 AI chips together to run as one computer. Many firms can assemble the racks, but lasers for the optical links were scarce in 2026.

Who leads

  • Nvidia USNVLink, InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet, which it credited for data center growth in the quarter to April 2026
  • Broadcom US$16.7B of AI semiconductor revenue in the quarter to August 2026, up 221%
  • Foxconn TWWorld's largest AI server provider, its chairman said in March 2026

China

Chinese firms such as InnoLight assemble high-speed optical modules in volume, at sites including Suzhou and, since 2019, Thailand. In February 2025 China put indium under new export restrictions. The same month it began requiring export permits for indium phosphide substrates, the wafers that lasers for optical links are grown on.

United States

Coherent broke ground in Sherman, Texas, in June 2026 on an expansion of its factory there, which makes optical devices from indium phosphide. In August 2026 Nvidia said that Wistron's new plant in Fort Worth, Texas, was producing its GB300 superchips and that Foxconn was building a factory in Houston.

Read the chapter, with its sources

15Stage 15 of 15

Data Centers and Power

High concentrationModerately hard to substitute

By mid-2026, companies had asked to connect about 474 GW of new demand to the Texas grid, mostly for data centers. Only about 205 GW of those requests already had the grid study needed to enter the grid operator's first review. The large transformers that connect such sites to the grid commonly took three years to arrive in 2024.

Who leads

  • GE Vernova USGas equipment, transformers and switchgear, including through Prolec GE
  • Hitachi Energy CHPower transformers and switchgear
  • Siemens Energy DEGrid technologies, transformers, turbines

China

China used 25 percent of the world's data center electricity in 2024, second to the United States, by the International Energy Agency's estimate. Data centers made up around 3 percent of the growth in China's electricity demand from 2022 to 2024.

United States

US factories supplied 29.2 percent of the large power transformers bought in the United States in 2023, measured by capacity. Constellation said in August 2026 that it expects to restart the Crane nuclear plant in 2027. Microsoft has agreed to buy the plant's power.

Read the chapter, with its sources

Across the chain

Two chapters that are not stages. They look across all fifteen, at what a chip costs and at the contest over who controls them.

16Across the chain

The Economics of AI Chips

Epoch AI estimated in December 2025 that Nvidia's B200 AI chip cost about $6,400 to build, mostly for memory and packaging. Its processor silicon cost about $900.

Epoch AI says Nvidia's margin on Blackwell may be lower than the gap between the B200's build cost and its selling price suggests. It cites reports from March 2024 that put the B200's selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip. Epoch AI notes that most Blackwell revenue comes from servers and rack-scale systems, which may carry lower margins.

Read the chapter, with its sources

17Across the chain

Who Controls the Chain

Since 2018 the United States has used export controls to limit China's access to advanced chips and chipmaking tools, and China has been learning to make both.

Japan and the Netherlands have aligned their own export controls with the American rules on chipmaking equipment. China has answered by building its own tools and by restricting sales of US chips in China. Chinese toolmakers supplied 35 percent of China's own chipmaking equipment market in 2025, up from 10 to 15 percent before 2022. Nvidia says the Chinese government restricted the sales of its H200 chip that the United States licensed in February 2026.

Read the chapter, with its sources

16 The Economics of AI Chips

Epoch AI estimated in December 2025 that Nvidia's B200 AI chip cost about $6,400 to build, mostly for memory and packaging. Its processor silicon cost about $900.

Epoch AI says Nvidia's margin on Blackwell may be lower than the gap between the B200's build cost and its selling price suggests. It cites reports from March 2024 that put the B200's selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip. Epoch AI notes that most Blackwell revenue comes from servers and rack-scale systems, which may carry lower margins.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/component-costs/

17 Who Controls the Chain

Since 2018 the United States has used export controls to limit China's access to advanced chips and chipmaking tools, and China has been learning to make both.

Japan and the Netherlands have aligned their own export controls with the American rules on chipmaking equipment. China has answered by building its own tools and by restricting sales of US chips in China. Chinese toolmakers supplied 35 percent of China's own chipmaking equipment market in 2025, up from 10 to 15 percent before 2022. Nvidia says the Chinese government restricted the sales of its H200 chip that the United States licensed in February 2026.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/geopolitics/

10 Memory and HBM

Extreme concentration · Hard to substitute

SK hynix, Samsung and Micron make nearly all high bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked memory beside AI chips. SK hynix took 63.2 percent of HBM revenue in 2025.

  • SK hynix South Korea. 63.2% of HBM revenue in 2025
  • Samsung South Korea. 19.3% of HBM revenue in 2025

China The Institute for Progress estimated in October 2025 that China would make virtually no HBM that year. Huawei said in September 2025 that its Ascend 950 chips would use two HBM designs of its own, without saying who would manufacture the memory.

United States Micron is the only American HBM maker. As of October 2026, License Exception HBM lets US and allied exporters ship HBM below 3.3 GB per second per square millimeter without a license, including to China when the chip designer buys it directly and it goes straight to the packaging site.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/memory-and-hbm/

11 Advanced Packaging

Extreme concentration · Moderately hard to substitute

Epoch AI estimates that in 2025 Nvidia, Google, AMD and Amazon used around 90 percent of the capacity for CoWoS, TSMC's packaging for AI chips.

  • TSMC Taiwan. CoWoS packaging used by Nvidia, Google, AMD and Amazon in 2025
  • Intel United States. Foveros 3D packaging in volume at Rio Rancho, New Mexico, since January 2024

China Chinese firms had 5.3 percent of the market for fabrication tools built for advanced packaging in 2025, by CSET's analysis of TechInsights data. Between 2019 and 2024 they gained 5 percentage points of share in test tools but lost share in bonding and other conventional assembly and packaging tools.

United States Intel opened Fab 9 in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, in January 2024 to make its Foveros 3D packages in volume. Amkor broke ground in October 2025 on a $7B packaging and test campus in Peoria, Arizona, and expects production to start in early 2028.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/advanced-packaging/

12 Substrates and PCBs

Extreme concentration · Hard to substitute

Ajinomoto, a Japanese food company, told investors in June 2026 that it holds over 95 percent of the market for the insulating film inside high-end chip packages.

  • Ajinomoto Japan. Told investors in June 2026 that its build-up film has held over 95% of its market since launch
  • Nitto Boseki Japan. Claimed an overwhelming advantage in low thermal expansion glass in its 2025 integrated report

China TTM, an American circuit board maker, said in its annual report for 2025 that its circuit board competitors are mostly based in China and Taiwan. Nitto Boseki, a Japanese glass fiber maker, said in its 2025 integrated report that Chinese and Taiwanese companies are aggressively catching up with it in the special glass sector.

United States The White House's 2021 supply chain review listed no American firm among the key substrate makers. In December 2024 the US Commerce Department finalized an award of up to $75 million to Absolics, an affiliate of Korea's SKC, for a glass substrate plant in Covington, Georgia.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/substrates-and-pcbs/

13 Test and Assembly

High concentration · Moderately hard to substitute

Testing finds bad chips before they go into an expensive package. Japan's Advantest took about 65 percent of 2025 spending on chip testers, by its own estimate.

  • Advantest Japan. About 65% of the tester market in 2025, by its own estimate
  • Teradyne United States. $2.52bn of semiconductor test revenue in 2025, service included

China Georgetown's CSET, analyzing TechInsights data, finds that between 2019 and 2024 Chinese toolmakers gained 5 percentage points of world market share in test tools and 4 points in fabrication tools built for advanced packaging. But they lost share in bonding and other conventional assembly and packaging tools.

United States American firms held 23.5 percent of the market for test tools in 2025 and Japanese firms 63.0 percent, by CSET's analysis of TechInsights data. Amkor raised its planned investment in an Arizona packaging and test campus to $7 billion in October 2025. In June 2026 it announced a long-term partnership with TSMC, which will buy packaging and test services from it in Arizona.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/test-and-assembly/

14 Systems and Networking

High concentration · Moderately hard to substitute

Nvidia's and AMD's racks wire 72 AI chips together to run as one computer. Many firms can assemble the racks, but lasers for the optical links were scarce in 2026.

  • Nvidia United States. NVLink, InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet, which it credited for data center growth in the quarter to April 2026
  • Broadcom United States. $16.7B of AI semiconductor revenue in the quarter to August 2026, up 221%

China Chinese firms such as InnoLight assemble high-speed optical modules in volume, at sites including Suzhou and, since 2019, Thailand. In February 2025 China put indium under new export restrictions. The same month it began requiring export permits for indium phosphide substrates, the wafers that lasers for optical links are grown on.

United States Coherent broke ground in Sherman, Texas, in June 2026 on an expansion of its factory there, which makes optical devices from indium phosphide. In August 2026 Nvidia said that Wistron's new plant in Fort Worth, Texas, was producing its GB300 superchips and that Foxconn was building a factory in Houston.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/systems-and-networking/

15 Data Centers and Power

High concentration · Moderately hard to substitute

By mid-2026, companies had asked to connect about 474 GW of new demand to the Texas grid, mostly for data centers. Only about 205 GW of those requests already had the grid study needed to enter the grid operator's first review. The large transformers that connect such sites to the grid commonly took three years to arrive in 2024.

  • GE Vernova United States. Gas equipment, transformers and switchgear, including through Prolec GE
  • Hitachi Energy Switzerland. Power transformers and switchgear

China China used 25 percent of the world's data center electricity in 2024, second to the United States, by the International Energy Agency's estimate. Data centers made up around 3 percent of the growth in China's electricity demand from 2022 to 2024.

United States US factories supplied 29.2 percent of the large power transformers bought in the United States in 2023, measured by capacity. Constellation said in August 2026 that it expects to restart the Crane nuclear plant in 2027. Microsoft has agreed to buy the plant's power.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/data-centers-and-power/
